references.text: Moses again expresses his feeling of inadequacy before God, this time by pointing to his lack of eloquence.
Moses repeats his objection that he is not worthy of the task and asks how Pharaoh would listen to him.
Gideon expresses similar humility and self-doubt when God calls him to save Israel.
Saul shows the same type of humility when he is appointed king, pointing out that he comes from the smallest tribe.
David expresses similar humility when he asks 'Who am I?' in light of God's promises.
Isaiah feels unworthy in God's presence and acknowledges his own inadequacy when called.
Jeremiah expresses similar resistance to the call by saying that he is too young and cannot speak.
Stephen refers to Moses' calling and mission to lead the children of Israel out of Egypt.
Paul asks a similar question about who is fit for service, reflecting Moses' feeling of inadequacy.
Paul acknowledges that our fitness does not come from ourselves but from God, which answers Moses' question about who he is.
God's command in 6:29 serves as the direct theological answer to Moses' doubt about his own identity in 3:11.
